title: Add lightweight CI curator and staged merge protector
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: developer feedback shows long presubmit start times and noisy merge storms during our daily release windows. This PR introduces a lightweight CI curator service that reduces cold presubmit startup by lazily loading toolchain artifacts and a staged merge protector that coordinates quiet windows for high-risk merges. The changeset is intentionally small and focused: a compact toolchain loader (Go), a presubmit cache compressor, a merge sequencer hook in the release coordinator, and updated docs + sanity checks.

What this does (high level):
- Introduces ci/curator/compact_loader.go: lazy toolchain loader that prefers local lightweight images and fetches large artifacts async. Reduces presubmit init time by ~35% in local dev profiles in our internal benchmarks.
- Adds ci/cache/compressor.go: on-presubmit cache compaction to reduce CI archive size and speed up cache upload/download for ephemeral runners. Compressor is conservative: it keeps build outputs needed for deterministic tests and prunes large optional artifacts.
- Adds release/merge_sequencer.go: small orchestration hook that enforces a staged quiet window (configurable) for a short period after high-risk merges (e.g., runtime, infra, release scripts). This reduces merge collisions and provides a deterministic window for canary smoke checks.
- Wire-up: updates .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to optionally start the curator, and release workflows to call the merge sequencer when the PR is labelled release/needs-quiesce.
- Docs: docs/ci/curator.md and docs/ci/merge-windows.md with operator instructions and tuning knobs.

Commits summary: (3 commits)
1) Add compact toolchain loader and compressor (Maya Patel) — initial implementation and unit tests.
2) Wire presubmit workflows to use the curator and add feature flags (Maya Patel) — CI-only toggle and rollout notes.
3) Add merge sequencer hook and docs, fix race in compressor snapshot code (Maya Patel) — tests + minor cleanup.

Testing & results: unit tests added for loader/compressor and integration smoke that simulates cache upload/download. Internal perf run shows ~35% reduced presubmit setup in dev profile and median CI artifact size reduction ~28% for node/python toolchains. Staging job ran nightly for 48 hours without regression.

Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag CI_CURATOR_ENABLED=false by default. We will flip on for infra and SDK teams first, monitor presubmit latency and cache hit rates, then expand to repo-wide over two weeks. Merge sequencer is opt-in via label release/needs-quiesce and default configuration is 3-minute quiet window.

Why this is safe: no breaking API changes, default behavior unchanged unless feature flags or labels are used. Compressor is conservative and reversible; we added a dry-run mode. Merge sequencer only orchestrates merges and performs no destructive actions; all operations are logged/audited.

Related Linear items: ENG-4321 (presubmit-performance), ENG-4400 (release-merge-safety).

review_thread: Evan Chen: Please add a dry-run mode to the compressor to validate pruning without affecting existing caches. — Done in commit 3; added --dry-run flag and tests.

Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid running the curator for small fast changes (docs-only)? Add a path filter. — Added path filter to presubmit workflow to skip curator when only docs or markdown changes are present.

release_notes: Introduce optional lightweight CI curator (lazy toolchain loader) and presubmit cache compressor to reduce presubmit startup and cache sizes; add staged merge sequencer for configurable quiet windows during high-risk merges. Opt-in via CI_CURATOR_ENABLED and label release/needs-quiesce.
